q: Top Down Organizing is when you:
opts: Get the workers to vote in an election.
Meet with the owner of a company and talk about the benefit of unions.
Your plan has a rank system starting with top goals first.
When you plan a pizza party at a company.
evidence: Ungraded sheet of another student (msg_3247), his pick b; verified: Wikipedia "Union organizer" (top-down organizing persuades management, bottom-up focuses on workers; top-down is practiced more in construction); Operating Engineers Local 3 (oe3.org) — organizers mainly use top-down organizing, signing contractors.

q: Bottom up Organizing is when you:
opts: Wait for the phone to ring in the office.
When a company moves to a new state.
When a company fires half of their workers.
Have workers come together to talk about forming a union.
evidence: Ungraded sheet of another student (msg_3247), his pick d; verified: Wikipedia "Union organizer" (bottom-up organizing focuses on the workers, usually through a labor board certification process).

opts: Using both Top-Down and Bottom up tactics.
Showing off the JATC training.
The use of hand billing, bannering, and Pickets.
All of the Above
evidence: Ungraded sheet of another student (msg_3247), his pick d — the only basis. No course source found. Supporting: Union Roofers organizing guide (unionroofers.com, 7_1Q12p18.pdf) — top-down and bottom-up campaigns can run at the same time; Stansbury Forum / Perusek (Building Trades Academy) — a strategic plan employs multiple tactical elements.

The right for secondary boycotts.

q: What Act was passed in 1935, that created a new independent agency, to enforce employee rights, to form and join unions, and it obligated employers to bargain collectively with unions selected by a majority of the employees in an appropriate bargaining unit?
opts: Taft-Hartley Act
The Second Amendment
The Franklin-Washington Act
The Wagner Act
evidence: Ungraded sheet of another student (msg_3248), his pick d; verified: NLRB "1935 Passage of the Wagner Act" (nlrb.gov/about-nlrb/who-we-are/our-history/1935-passage-of-the-wagner-act) — the question is worded almost verbatim from this page.

q: The Taft-Hartley Act made major changes to the Wagner Act. Select the option below that is false:
opts: Elimination of secondary boycotts.
Added Right to Work legislation.
Gave agricultural and domestic workers the right to organize.
Defined six additional unfair labor practices.
evidence: Ungraded sheet of another student (msg_3248), his pick c; verified: NLRB "1947 Taft-Hartley Substantive Provisions" (secondary boycotts prohibited; "Taft-Hartley defined six additional unfair labor practices"); NLRA text on nlrb.gov: §14(b) state right-to-work, §2(3) excludes agricultural laborers and domestic service.

opts: The rights for Americans to have a wine when they tend a garden.
The right to have union representation at investigatory interviews.
The reason that you get to have a break and lunch.
This right allows you to vote in a union election.
evidence: Ungraded sheet of another student (msg_3248), his pick b; verified: NLRB "Weingarten Rights" (nlrb.gov/about-nlrb/rights-we-protect/your-rights/weingarten-rights); NLRB v. J. Weingarten, Inc., 420 U.S. 251 (1975).

q: An employer who threatens to close a plant, or fire workers who engage in protected union activities has committed this...

The employers right as the owner.
Something to overlook.
A normal day.
evidence: Ungraded sheet of another student (msg_3248), his pick a; verified: NLRB "Interfering with employee rights (Section 7 & 8(a)(1))" — unlawful to "threaten employees with adverse consequences, such as closing the workplace" and to discharge employees for protected, concerted activities.
